summary: Code review PASS. RefreshIndexViewModel Dispose test correctly verifies event deregistration by firing SimulateStateChange after Dispose and asserting IsRunning stays false. MainContentViewModel Dispose test validates cascade disposal (parent disposes child VM) behaviorally — elegant use of the observable IsRunning property as a proxy for handler registration state. Production Dispose implementations are minimal and correct. No blocking issues, no fix-forward changes required.

comments.note: The MainContentViewModel Dispose test implicitly validates cascade disposal: sut.Dispose() calls RefreshIndex?.Dispose(), which unregisters RefreshIndexViewModel.OnStateChanged from the orchestrator. Verifying sut.RefreshIndex.IsRunning stays false after SimulateStateChange is an elegant behavioural proof of cascade disposal without exposing internals. Clean design.

Both tests use synchronous [Fact] (not async), which is appropriate since all code paths (Dispose, SimulateStateChange, IsRunning getter) are synchronous. No Task.Yield needed here unlike the fire-and-forget paths in OnRefreshStateChanged.
No blocking or structural observations — both tests are minimal, descriptive (because: clause), and provide strong regression coverage for the event deregistration memory-safety contract.
